newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cargill soybeans may not reach U.S.-Brazil traders.
newsitem.headline: Cargill soybeans may not reach U.S.-Brazil traders.

text.p: A highly-publicized deal by Cargill to import Brazilian soybeans into the U.S. in exchange for exports later in the year may never take place, Brazilian traders said.

News of the move last week sparked a sell-off in soybean futures on Chicago Board of Trade, but this week rumors began to circulate that Cargill would not ship the beans or would divert them elsewhere.
"There's talk that Cargill is not shipping those beans," a trader said.
However, the company denied the deal had fallen through.
"Nothing has changed," said Cargill spokeswoman Linda Thrane. "We won't be discussing the details of the transaction. That's a matter of policy on all our transactions."
That Cargill had made the deal so public last week had raised suspicions about whether it would go through, traders said.
One broker said he did not believe the trade was bogus, but added the beans might never arrive in the U.S. if prices make it more profitable to send them elsewhere.
"To announce something like that, they obviously wanted some reaction to that," he said. "The product is being shipped but there is talk that the beans might never actually get there."
